scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is being an asshole (AITA) for lying to their boyfriend about his ex-girlfriend. Let me break this down step by step. First, the situation: They're a college senior, and they've been dating their boyfriend for four months. The boyfriend had been dating another girl for two years, and they broke up because he suspected she was cheating. The user had a crush on him for a long time and now they're together. The user was at a party where the ex was rumored to have danced and kissed another guy. The user didn't see the ex at the party because they were in different social circles, but when the boyfriend asked if they saw her, they lied and said they did, which helped the boyfriend move on faster. So, the question is: Is the user the asshole for lying? I think the first thing to consider is the intent behind the lie. The user's intention was to help the boyfriend feel better and move on from the breakup. They were seeing him still hurt and wanted a fresh start. That seems like a good intention, right? They didn't want him to be stuck in the past. But then, lying is generally considered wrong because it breaks trust. Trust is a fundamental part of any relationship. If the boyfriend found out the truth, he might feel betrayed, especially if he's built his feelings of closure on a lie. That could damage the relationship more than the initial hurt. Another angle is the impact of the lie. The user says the boyfriend is happier now and has no regrets. So, in the short term, the lie seems to have had a positive effect. But what about the long term? If the truth comes out, it could cause more pain than the initial breakup. The boyfriend might feel that he can't trust the user, which could lead to bigger issues. Also, the user mentions that there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. That makes me think that they're aware of the potential consequences of coming clean. But just because there's nothing to gain doesn't mean it's the right thing to do. Sometimes, doing the right thing is harder, even if it doesn't seem beneficial in the short term. I'm also considering the boyfriend's perspective. He's using the lie to feel justified in the breakup. If he found out that the user lied, he might feel that his closure was based on a false premise. That could make him question other aspects of the relationship and his trust in the user. On the other hand, maybe the user felt they had no choice at the time. They were trying to help someone they care about, and the lie seemed like the only way to do that. But even so, lying is a serious issue. It's possible that the user could have found another way to support the boyfriend without resorting to deception. I'm also thinking about the concept of manipulation here. By lying, the user is manipulating the boyfriend's emotions to achieve a desired outcome. Manipulation can be harmful because it doesn't respect the other person's autonomy to process their feelings honestly. In summary, while the user's intent was to help, lying undermines trust and can have negative long-term consequences. It's a tough spot because the user wanted the best for their relationship, but the method they chose might not be the healthiest approach.
